Day 2 of 8Easy night

Thursday

October 22

Land, bathhouse, monja

Haneda, Akihabara, Kinshicho, Tsukishima

  1. 2:15 PM, land at Haneda. Train to Nohga Hotel Akihabara: 51 minutes to JR Akihabara (¥480), then 6 minutes on foot. Drop the bags and rest.

    Route in Maps
  2. 01Evening

    Koganeyu

    Remodeled neighborhood bathhouse with a sauna, a big cold plunge, and a beer bar with a DJ booth for after.

    11 AM to 12:30 AM¥600 + ¥550 sauna
    Google MapsWebsite
    Read more
    From Akihabara, the JR Sobu local three stops to Kinshicho, then 6 minutes on foot from the north exit. The bath is ¥600 for 90 minutes; the men's sauna is ¥550 more on weekdays (2 hours), and the big cold plunge is in the sauna area, so get the sauna. Tattoos are fine. Last order at the bar is midnight. Closed only on the 2nd and 4th Mondays.
  3. After dark
  4. 02Dinner

    Tsukishima Monja Street

    Tokyo's own griddle dish, cooked on the iron plate in your table. Over 80 monja shops on one street.

    Lines around 6 PM
    Google MapsWebsite
    Read more
    Moheji Honten (weekdays 5 to 11 PM) takes reservations. Monkichi puts its average at ¥3,000 to ¥4,000 a head. Takenoko is the shop a Jungle Pocket comedian took over from his mom.

Senso-ji, Akihabara, Tokyo Tower, Ginza

Asakusa, Akihabara, Azabudai, Ginza

  1. First thing, check out, Nohga holds the bags. Leave the bags at the desk. Suehirocho on the Ginza line is 4 minutes from the hotel and runs straight to Asakusa.

    Senso-ji and Azuma Bridge

    Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple, up Nakamise's 90-odd shops, then the bridge over the Sumida toward Skytree.

    Route in Maps
  10. 042:30 PM

    Azabudai Hills

    Tokyo's newest megaproject: Heatherwick Studio's curving garden canopy at street level, and a free observation lobby on the 33rd floor of the tallest tower in Japan.

    FreeKamiyacho Station
    Google MapsWebsite
    Read more
    Opened November 2023. Pelli Clarke designed the towers; Heatherwick's canopy covers the central plaza. The 33rd-floor Sky Lobby was free at opening, but a 2024 report says it is now limited to tenants and cafe customers; ask at the desk, and if it's closed to you the plaza and the shops are the stop. Tokyo Tower is a 10-minute walk from here.
  11. On the way

    Zojo-ji

    The Tokugawa family temple at the foot of Tokyo Tower; the big gate with the tower behind it is the photo. Walk through its grounds to the tower.

    Kosugiyu

    Google MapsWebsite

    A registered national cultural property. Four tubs: a milk bath (41°C), a 44°C hot bath with mugwort, yuzu or hiba cypress (changed daily), a jet bath, and a 16 to 19°C cold bath. Towels ¥100 to ¥200; soap and shampoo provided. 5 min from Koenji Station, north exit. Last entry 1 AM. Its site says nothing about tattoos either way.

  18. 08Optionaloptional

    An only-in-Japan party

    Three picks: Kawaii Monster Land's Halloween, MIDNIGHT STELLAR at ZEROTOKYO, or TOKYO DECADANCE.

    Google Maps
    Read more
    Kawaii Monster Land, "The Halloween Monster" (Harajuku): Monster Girls stage shows, DJs and dress-up; book a 60-minute slot (¥2,800 to ¥3,500), open until 9:40 PM. MIDNIGHT STELLAR at ZEROTOKYO (Kabukicho, 11 PM, so a taxi home): TAKU INOUE, Moe Shop, PSYQUI, DÉ DÉ MOUSE and others; ¥3,500 fast pass, ¥4,000 door; crowd unknown. TOKYO DECADANCE HALLOWEEN (S Nightclub, Shibuya, since 2005): cabaret, cosplay, otaku and live-act floors, 9:30 PM to 5 AM, ¥5,000 door, ¥3,500 to ¥4,500 in costume.
  19. 095:30 PMoptional

    Tokyo Bay fireworks

    About 12,000 shells off Harumi Pier, 5:30 to 7 PM, back for the first time in 11 years. Tickets only.

    Google Maps
    Read more
    Every viewing spot is ticketed (¥5,000 to ¥10,000 on Ticket Pia, no refunds, sales end 10 AM Saturday, none at the gate), and you can't stop on a sidewalk to watch; there is no free viewing area. As of Thursday night the Harumi and Minato areas were sold out and Toyosu and Ariake still had seats (a fan blog, not Pia itself). Going means leaving Koenji right after the parade. Even if you skip it: expect crowds around Toyosu tonight.

Day 7 of 8Day trip

Tuesday

October 27

Hakone ropeway, Fuji Motorsports Museum

Hakone, Gotemba, Shinjuku

  1. 10:00 AM, romancecar to Hakone-Yumoto. From Shinjuku, arrives 11:27 AM. Reserve the seat ahead. Buy the Hakone Freepass from Shinjuku (¥7,100, 2 days): it covers the Tozan line, cable car, ropeway, Lake Ashi cruise and the Odakyu highway bus to Gotemba; the Romancecar seat is extra on top.

    Route in Maps
  2. 01Midday

    Hakone Ropeway over Owakudani

    Over the volcanic valley to Lake Ashi. Get off at Owakudani on the way.

    ¥2,000 one wayAbout 30 min
    Google MapsWebsite
    Read more
    Mountain train and cable car up to Sounzan first. Ropeway 9 AM to 5 PM. Through Nov 3 the Sounzan to Owakudani section also runs a special Rose Gondola. Volcanic gas or weather can stop it on the day, so check hakonenavi.jp that morning.
  3. At Owakudani

    Black eggs

    Eggs boiled in the sulfur springs come out black; local lore says each one adds seven years to your life. Sold at Kurotamagokan by the station, about ¥500 for a pack of four or five.

    About ¥500
    Google Maps
  4. At Owakudani

    Hakone Geomuseum

    Small volcano museum beside the vents, for the 20 minutes while the eggs cool.

    9 AM to 4 PM
    Google Maps
  5. Skip

    Lake Ashi pirate ship

    The cruise is about 30 minutes each way and Hakone Shrine's lake torii is on the far shore, so it doesn't fit before the 1:55 bus. Look at the lake from Togendai instead.

    Google Maps

  6. 1:55 PM, bus to Gotemba. Togendai to Gotemba Station, arrives 2:35 PM. ¥1,080, pay on board.

    Route in Maps
  7. 023 PM

    Fuji Motorsports Museum

    About 40 historic race cars beside Fuji Speedway. Taxi about 20 minutes from Gotemba.

    ¥1,200 to ¥1,80010 AM to 5 PM, last entry 4:30
    Google MapsWebsite
    Read more
    10 carmakers take part. Its booking page shows adults at ¥1,200; an earlier page said ¥1,800. The Fan Terrace cafe is open without a museum ticket. Want a Hakone hot spring too? Do it the other way round: Fujisan 10:40 AM to Gotemba, the museum, the 3:20 PM bus to Togendai and the ropeway before 5, a bath at Hakone-Yumoto, and the 7:50 PM Romancecar home. Everything hangs on that 3:20 bus, which comes through Tomei roadworks and can't be reserved.

Day 8 of 8Travel

Wednesday

October 28

Fly home

Haneda to Atlanta

DL294Same day
HND4:50 PMATL4:17 PM
Details

Winter-schedule times, later than before, so the morning is free. Leave Shinjuku by about 2 PM: Haneda Terminal 3 is 46 minutes on the Yamanote and the Keikyu (¥580). Be at the gate by 3:50 PM. Thursday's DL294 is the backup; Lars works Friday 10/30. Last morning: the Isetan basement food hall opens at 10 for gifts to take home; Terminal 3's open-air observation deck (5F, 6:30 AM to 10 PM) is a good last half hour.

Soren: Duke spring registration opens 8:30 AM ET today, which is 9:30 PM in Tokyo, about four and a half hours into this flight. Neuroradiology (RADIOL 421C sec 41) has 2 seats and no waitlist, so enroll from the plane's Wi-Fi if it has any. The calendar backup now fires at 4:45 PM ET, after you land.
